component.name: Keymasq
component.summary: Keyboard and mouse remapper with GUI configuration, per-window profiles, and macros

description.p: Keyboard and mouse remapper with GUI configuration, per-window profiles, and macros.

Keymasq supports keyboard, mouse, and gamepad remapping with layered profiles, window-aware activation, macros, superkeys, and combos. Use it for workflows like a Linux autoclicker, game auto-fire, app-specific shortcuts, and multi-step automation.
Adds on-press and on-release pulse actions to overload superkeys.
Adds a live diagnostics dialog in the GUI for monitoring keymasqd latency snapshots.
Also adds diagnostics category filtering, reset controls, a docs link, and live refresh status, while package upgrades now restart services.
Adds a feedback dialog for submitting bugs, ideas, or questions, with optional diagnostics.
Also moves profile settings into a dedicated dialog with per-device grab toggles, improves CLI and macro responsiveness, and refreshes device mapping card polish.
Honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME instead of always using the default user config directory.
First public release, with Fedora COPR and AUR packaging now available.
Adds small cosmetic polish alongside internal fixes and restructuring.
Fixes documentation links so they point to version-aware keymasq.tools URLs.
Adds profile lifecycle macros and compositor actions in macro timelines.
Also improves primary mouse button remap warnings and several key selector, input picker, device tab, macro dialog, and Super Key dialog layouts.
Adds support for 0 ms hold times in type actions and a dedicated media remapping tab.
Adds guided GNOME setup dialogs, DBus bridge detection, and clearer recovery when GNOME integration needs setup, restart, or logout.

Also adds a Ctrl+Alt+Esc emergency combo where one tap cancels macro playback and a double tap triggers an emergency reset, improves macro recording saves and storage, applies newly created profiles immediately, and allows zero-hold rapidfire timing.
Adds device renaming in device tabs.
Adds ad hoc macro CLI commands for one-off macro playback and compilation.
Also removes the extra dialog before the recording Polkit prompt.
Adds scroll wheel remapping and scroll wheel combo support.
Also improves macro recording and saving flows, moves superkey mappings into a dedicated selector tab, and adds Unicode support for type macros.
Adds native cursor positioning for GNOME and X11 so absolute pointer moves work directly on those desktops instead of falling back to the virtual mouse path.
